title: Mizuho flags a later reset behind its November variable-rate headline
summary: Mizuho links its 2 November short-prime revision to a conditional July 2027 mortgage reset. The starting rate is not a full-term promise.

takeaways.text: Read the bank's future-reset note alongside its advertised starting rate.

sections.heading: The dated qualification
sections.text: Mizuho says borrowing by 31 March 2027 at its displayed variable rate from 1.275% p.a. leads to a rate from 1.525% for July 2027 repayments, reflecting the 2 November 2026 short-prime revision. Further short-prime revisions by 1 April 2027 would also be reflected. Discounts depend on application details and underwriting; these are conditional published figures, not guaranteed quotes.

sections.heading: Interest resets and payment reviews differ
sections.text: Mizuho's explainer describes April/October rate reviews for existing borrowing, reflected in July/January repayments. Its five-year and 125% payment rules apply to equal-payment variable loans. They do not cap interest rates: interest can take a larger share of an unchanged payment, and unpaid interest remaining at maturity must be repaid together.

sections.heading: What this means for a budget
sections.text: Ask for the applicable reset date, discount and repayment schedule for your own contract. Do not extend a starting percentage across the whole loan or apply this bank's rules to every Japanese lender. This reviewed research creates no confirmed promotion or all-in JPY borrowing-cost comparison; loan limits, LTV, residency, property use, insurance, fees and early-repayment conditions remain unverified here.

sections.heading: Source dates and scope
sections.text: Checked and written on 8 November, this records an earlier notice. The mortgage page labels its rate panel 1 November and its footer 2 November 2026; the latter is stored as documentDate, not a proven first-publication date. The mechanics page is dated 3 September. No single offer-validity period is established.
